The biggest error in this blog post is the order for apprenticeship stages, and even that isn't that big an error. Below is a summary of the stages a geiko will have gone through, just because work is pretty quiet today!

  • Shikomi: A girl will be a shikomi, effectively a servant, for a period of 6 months or so. This is to get used to the routine and the guidance of the okami-san (mother figure and owner of the okiya).

  • Minarai: Once a girl has learned to sit, stand and walk properly, and has picked up the Kyokotoba dialect, her hair will be done in the wareshinobu style and she will become a minarai, a watching apprentice. She will be dressed in a standard furisode (ankle length) at first, with an obi in the han-darari musubi (half length knot). Her ensemble will be showy and bright! She wears oshiroi (white makeup) for the first time, with pink for contouring. She wears red around her eyes but no eyeliner or mascara, and no lipstick on her upper lip. She wears many kanzashi (hairpins) in her hair, a shidare kanzashi (long dangling hairpin seen on every henshin), and frequently they wear kanzashi featuring pinwheels. At the end of this stage is reasonably common to see girls wearing hikizuri kimono (longer length) and darari musubi.

  • Misedashi: Once the okami-san thinks a girl is ready to debut, she will have her misedashi. This is her formal debut as a maiko. She wears special kanzashi made of tortoiseshell (or acrylic), as well as the silver streamer pins at the back and two bira kanzashi at the front. Again she wears lipstick only on her bottom lip, and no black eye makeup. She is lead around the kagai (geiko community) to introduce herself at the chaya (teahouses, last I heard there were 26 in Gion Kobu).

  • Junior maiko: As a first year maiko she wears a predominantly red eri collar and continues to wear dangling shidare kanzashi. When she finishes her 1st year, she stops wearing shidare kanzashi altogether. She starts putting lipstick on both her lips, and wearing black eye makeup. Her hikizuri is heavily patterned, too. As she becomes more experienced, her red eri will be embroidered with more white, and the pattern on her hikizuri will drift downwards.

  • Senior maiko: A maiko becomes a senior when her okami-san thinks she is ready, but generally 3 years after her misedashi. Her hairstyle changes to ofuku, and her collar is now fully embroidered with white. She wears less kanzashi than a junior maiko, and there is less pattern on her shoulders. She'll get to wear special hairstyles during festivals. For example, she'll wear a special hairstyle (one of the following: osafune, yuiwata, oshiyun, osome, suisha, oshidori no hina, kikugasane) for Setsubun, and she'll get to wear yakko shimada hairstyle for Shigyoushiki and Hassaku.

  • Pre-sakkou: A senior maiko nearing the end of her apprenticeship will start wearing a pre-sakkou hairstyle which will depend on which of the kagai she is from. Pontocho girls wear a Setsubun hairstyle (but not osome, yuiwata), whereas Gion Kobu girls wear yakko shimada. Generally semi-formal crested hikizuri kimono are worn too.

  • Sakkou: The final stage before erikae (graduation). A girl will wear the final maiko hairstyle, sakkou. What she wears differs depending on which kagai she is from:

  • Gion Kobu: black formal hikizuri with white collar, gold obi - Example
  • Gion Higashi: busy patterned hikizuri, red eri, gold obi - Example
  • Miyagawacho: black formal hikizuri with red collar Example
  • Pontocho: semi-formal hikizuri (dark blue, light blue, purple) with a less-busy pattern, red collar Example
  • Kamishichiken: bold coloured hikizuri (dark brown, light brown, light pink) with a less-busy pattern, red collar Example
  • Erikae: Graduation. Generally occurs 4-5 years after misedashi. The prospective geiko thanks her okami-san and her onee-san, and the top knot of her sakkou hairstyle is cut (the tail - a hairpiece). This is called danpatsu-shiki. She is dressed in her hikizuri (different to a maiko hiki, no shoulder tucks), and she puts on her katsura wig. After a small ceremony inside the okiya's chaya (tea house), she walks outside for the cameras and is lead around the kagai again to visit the tea houses, just like when she had her misedashi.
